You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Your line is back up. Here's the confirmation:

**Bill B1234321 — $65.00 — Status: Paid** ✅
**Line 555-123-2002 — Status: Active** ✅ (suspension cleared)

**One thing you need to do:** please **reboot your device** now. Your service won't reconnect until the phone restarts and re-registers on the network.

A couple of notes while I have your account open:
- **Bill B1002 — $150.00** (due 2025-02-19) is still **Issued** and unpaid. It's not overdue yet, but it's approaching, so you may want to take care of it to avoid another interruption.
- Your current plan on this line shows **8.7 GB used** this cycle. If data slows or drops, let me know and I can check your plan's limit and discuss refueling options.

Once you've rebooted, let me know if you're still seeing "No Service" and we'll troubleshoot further from there.

Airplane Mode is the culprit here — it turns off all your phone's wireless radios, which is why you have no signal bars even though the line is now active on our side.

**Please do this now:**

1. **Turn off Airplane Mode.** On most phones, swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings and tap the ✈️ **Airplane Mode** icon so it's off/gray. (Alternatively: Settings → Network & internet → Airplane mode → toggle Off.)
2. Wait a few seconds for the phone to reconnect, then check for signal bars.
3. If needed, **reboot the device** once more — this is the restart I mentioned earlier, and it's important since your line was just reactivated.

Since our records show your line is **Active** and roaming is enabled, you should get signal as soon as Airplane Mode is off.

Let me know what you see after that — whether you get signal bars and what network type appears (5G, 4G/LTE, etc.). If there's still no signal after turning Airplane Mode off and rebooting, I'll dig further into it with you.
turns.execution_output: User: Turning airplane mode off now.

turns.thought:
I understand the frustration, and you've done everything right so far. Let me walk you through a couple more device-level checks.

**Please try this, in order:**

1. **Turn mobile data ON.** Go to Settings → Network & internet → **Mobile network** (or "SIMs") and toggle **Mobile data** to On. On many phones there's also a "Mobile data" tile in Quick Settings when you swipe down from the top.

2. **Reseat your SIM card.** The most common cause of a persistent "No Service" is a SIM that isn't seated properly. Power the phone off, eject the SIM tray, take the SIM out, wipe it gently, reinsert it firmly, and power the phone back on. I can also trigger a SIM reseat from my side if you'd prefer — just say the word.

3. **Check that the SIM isn't locked.** If your phone is asking for a PIN or PUK code, that will block service. Let me know if you see any such prompt.

A few quick questions so I can narrow this down:

- Does the status bar show any **network type** at all next to the bars — e.g. "5G," "LTE," "4G" — or is it completely blank?
- Is the ✈️ **Airplane Mode** icon definitely gone now?
- Are you currently in your normal home coverage area, or somewhere unusual (basement, rural area, traveling)?

One reassuring note from my side: your line **555-123-2002** is confirmed **Active**, the overdue bill is **Paid**, and roaming is enabled — so there's no account-level block left. That means this is almost certainly a device setting or SIM seating issue, which we can resolve.

Try those steps and tell me what changes. If there's still no signal after the data toggle and SIM reseat, I'll escalate you to our technical support team for hands-on help.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn mobile data on first.

turns.thought:
Yes, go ahead — the SIM reseat is quick and harmless. **Power the phone off first**, eject the tray, take the SIM out, reinsert it firmly, then power back on.

Here's the thing though: there's a contradiction in what your phone is reporting. You've turned mobile data ON, but the status bar still says **"Data Disabled."** That points away from a simple toggle issue and toward the phone's network configuration — specifically the **APN settings**, which tell your phone how to connect to our mobile data network.

**So after the SIM reseat, please do this:**

1. Open **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Access Point Names (APN)**.
2. Look at the current APN and tell me what it shows — in particular whether it displays **"Incorrect"** or whether the **MMSC** field is blank.
3. If there's a **Reset to default** option (often in the ⋮ menu), tap it.
4. **Reboot the device** afterward — the APN reset won't fully take effect until you restart.

While you're in there, also check **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Preferred network mode** and make sure it isn't set to **2G** or **3G** — set it to **5G/4G (auto)** if so.

Do the reseat first, then the APN reset plus reboot, and let me know what the APN screen showed and whether any bars appear.

If we still have no signal after that, I won't keep putting you through steps — I'll escalate you directly to our technical support team with your account details already attached, so they can run deeper network-side diagnostics. You've already confirmed the line is active and the bill is paid, so we've ruled out everything on the account side.
turns.execution_output: User: Doing the SIM reseat now.

turns.thought:
Yes — **definitely reset it**. "Broken" is not a valid APN, and that would explain both the "No Signal" / no network type and the "Data Disabled" message. Go ahead and tap **Reset to default**.

Two important things:

1. **Make sure you reboot the device after resetting.** The new APN settings won't take effect until the phone restarts — this is the step people most often skip, and the fix won't stick without it.
2. After the reboot, check the status bar **within a minute or two** — you should see signal bars plus a network type (5G, LTE, or 4G) return.

One thing to keep in mind: on most phones the **Reset to default** option isn't on the main APN list screen — it's hidden in the **⋮ (three-dot) menu** in the top-right corner. If you don't see it, tap there.

Once the phone comes back up, tell me:
- Whether you now have **signal bars** and what **network type** shows
- What the **APN name** reads now (it should show a valid carrier name rather than "broken")
- Whether **mobile data** is working (try loading a web page or sending a picture message)

If the APN comes back correct and signal returns, we're done. If it still shows "broken" or you still have no signal after the reboot, don't do anything else — I'll escalate you straight to our technical support team with your line and bill details already verified, so they can run deeper diagnostics from their side.
turns.execution_output: User: Resetting the APN to default now.
